subject: Economics
description: GDP, GNP, NNP, per-capita income, base year

questions.stem: The money value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year is the:
questions.explanation: GDP — production within the geographical boundaries of a country, regardless of whether the producer is domestic or foreign. GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA). NFIA = income Indians earn abroad − income foreigners earn in India. India typically has negative NFIA (more money goes out as repatriated MNC profits than comes in via NRIs), so GNP < GDP.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Net National Product (NNP) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: NNP = GNP − depreciation of capital. Depreciation represents wear and tear of existing capital used up in production. 'Net' means 'after subtracting depreciation'. NNP at factor cost = 'National Income' (the income accruing to factors of production — labour, capital, entrepreneurship). NNP at market price = NNP at factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: In India, national income statistics are compiled by the:
questions.explanation: The Central Statistics Office — reorganised in 2019 as the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation) — compiles national income accounts. P. C. Mahalanobis is often called the architect of India's official statistics (he founded ISI and the NSSO). NITI Aayog is the planning think-tank (replaced the Planning Commission in 2015). RBI compiles monetary and financial statistics.

questions.stem: The difference between 'nominal GDP' and 'real GDP' is that:

options.option_text: Nominal is for goods, real is for services
Nominal uses current-year prices, real uses base-year prices
Nominal is for India, real is for the world

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP = measured at current-year (market) prices — inflated by price changes. Real GDP = measured at constant prices of a chosen base year — strips out inflation. Real growth rate is the most widely reported measure of economic growth. The GDP deflator = (Nominal / Real) × 100 is itself an inflation measure. India's current base year is 2011-12; a revision to 2020-21 or 2022-23 is being prepared.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Per capita income of a country is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Per capita income = National Income / Population. Gives the average income per person per year. India's nominal per capita income was about ₹2.0 lakh in 2023-24 (approximately US$ 2,500). Rich countries often measure it at PPP (purchasing-power parity) as well — on that basis India is higher (~US$ 10,000 at PPP). Per capita income masks inequality — a Gini coefficient or decile distribution supplements it.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which method does NOT measure national income?

options.option_text: Nielsen survey of consumer brand preference

questions.explanation: Three equivalent approaches to national income — (i) Production / value-added method — sum of value added at each stage of output. (ii) Income method — sum of factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit). (iii) Expenditure method — sum of C + I + G + (X−M). All three must, in principle, give the same total. Consumer brand surveys are market-research tools, not national-income accounting.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The first estimate of India's national income was prepared by:
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji — 'Grand Old Man of India' — gave the first estimate of India's national income in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), using it to articulate the 'Drain Theory'. The first scientific estimate came from V. K. R. V. Rao in 1931-32. Mahalanobis designed the National Income Committee (1949) and India's planning models. D. R. Gadgil was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.
